description:
We are a multidisciplinary team driven by curiosity, creativity, and a shared passion for science and technology. 

We believe that innovation begins by asking questions and exploring new possibilities. By combining our technical skills, creativity, and different perspectives, we aim to transform challenges into accessible solutions.

Through NASA Space Apps Challenge, we seek to explore the potential of open science, collaborate, and develop ideas that can make a positive impact on Earth and beyond.
summary: We developed LISTAR, a public web application that transforms NASA’s SPHEREx infrared telescope data into an interactive visual and musical experience. Directly addressing the "Planet X and SPHEREx" challenge, LISTAR lets users enter any celestial coordinates (RA/Dec) or object name to play real calibrated SPHEREx frames as a video and detect moving objects. Because SPHEREx uses linear variable filters across 102 infrared bands, sequential frames naturally flicker even for stationary sources. LISTAR solves this core technical hurdle by blinking frames across seasons at matching wavelengths, comparing measured positions against propagated Gaia DR3 predictions and SkyBoT asteroid catalogs, and running a transparent rule-based verdict engine. Beyond motion detection, LISTAR bridges scientific exploration and public outreach across seven experiences, including a 3D orbital globe, a sky time machine, mobile augmented reality, and deterministic 102-band algorithmic sonification. This makes massive multi-spectral datasets accessible and understandable to everyone, combining rigorous scientific integrity with engaging visual and musical discovery.
details:
LISTAR is a bilingual (English/Spanish) web platform that turns NASA’s SPHEREx infrared telescope data into an interactive visual, analytical, and musical experience across seven modules. In its core Explore view, users enter coordinates (RA/Dec) or object names to play real calibrated SPHEREx frames as a video and detect moving objects. Because SPHEREx uses linear variable filters across 102 bands, Listar blinks matching wavelengths across 6-month observing seasons to separate color shifts from true motion, overlaying Gaia DR3 predictions, SkyBoT asteroids, and a rule-based verdict engine. Users can also explore a 3D orbital globe, a historical planetarium with VR, and mobile AR sky overlays.

Instead of generative AI, LISTARuses deterministic algorithmic sonification to translate real astrophysical spectra into structured music. Star Symphony (/symphony) maps all 102 infrared bands onto a pentatonic scale where spectral slope sets the musical key, brightness controls volume, and molecular absorption signatures—such as water ice ($3.0\ \mu\text{m}$) and $\text{CO}_2$ ($4.27\ \mu\text{m}$)—trigger crystalline voices exportable as MIDI or WAV. Your Sky Song (/song) composes a reproducible melody from the local zenith spectrum of any chosen date and place alongside a printable poster with a custom QR code. Meanwhile, Star Match (/match) splits microphone or uploaded audio into 102 frequency bands to find matching spectral shapes across 49,152 sky regions and harmonizes the star to the user’s song.

LISTAR'Sclient-heavy architecture offloads 3D rendering, HiPS tile decoding, audio synthesis, and spectral searches to the browser, keeping server costs low and ensuring fast responses even during external catalog outages via precomputed snapshots. By turning multi-spectral FITS archives into an intuitive visual and auditory tool, it lowers technical barriers for students and researchers while expanding public engagement. Its intended impact spans science education, dark-sky astrotourism, museum and planetarium installations, space sound design, and accessible astronomy by ear for visually impaired audiences.

Built with TypeScript, Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, astronomy-engine, Web Audio, WebXR, and custom zero-dependency encoders on Vercel, LISTAR pairs with a Python, FastAPI, Astropy, and NumPy backend running in Docker via Cloudflare Tunnel and automated CI/CD. It integrates NASA/IRSA SPHEREx (DR1/QR3), AWS S3, Gaia DR3, SkyBoT, Yale Bright Star, VizieR, and Sesame data, leveraging smartphone cameras, motion sensors, and VR headsets. Key factors considered include strict scientific integrity—clearly separating real data, computed models, and artistic audio while refusing to fabricate results—alongside on-device privacy for camera and microphone inputs and full English/Spanish localization.
